q.q: A trait that helps a plant survive in its environment is called what?
A cactus has thick pads and spines instead of big, flat leaves. How do these traits help it in the desert?
o: They help it grow in deep shade.
They help it float on water.
They help it save water in a dry place.
They help it catch more rain on wide leaves.

q.q: A trait that helps a plant in one place will always help it everywhere else, too.
What does a plant use to make its own food?
Two bean plants get the same soil and the same water. One grows by a sunny window, and one grows in a dark closet. After a week, the closet plant is pale and weak. What does this evidence show?
o: Plants grow best in the dark.
Soil is the only thing a plant needs.
Plants need light to grow well.

q.q: A seed is planted upside down. Which way will its root grow?
o: Down, because roots respond to gravity
Sideways, toward the wall of the pot
It will not grow at all.

q.q: A plant on a windowsill bends toward the window. In this response, what is the stimulus?
Which are ways that seeds travel away from their parent plant? Choose ALL that are correct.
o: The parent plant walks them to a new place

q.q: Ghost orchid seeds are as tiny as dust. Why are they seeds and not spores?
o: Each one has a tiny baby plant inside.

q.q: How are seeds and spores alike?
o: Both have a baby plant inside.
Both can grow into a new plant.
